caption: Storm rain actually falling at the timber house door (rain 0.62): the wind-laid meadow clumps now stop short of the stepping stones and the sill; still wrong: the frame is underexposed, the short sward still hides the edge pools, and the flags read as pale lumps.

Same storm at the timber house door after the lift: the storm frame reads a good stop brighter and the flags now sit in bare dark loam with the sward cleared off the pool band; still wrong: the flags read as smooth pale lumps and the pools barely show.
Brack, Edda's new black-and-white collie, sat on the green by the timber house; it reads as a dog but the tall meadow grass buries it and the low lens sits in the grass.
Edda's cottage at 22 h with fireflies, Brack lying down in his place by the door; still wrong: he is lost in the dark at the wall foot and the frame is murky blue-black.

Brack sat on the white cottage's trodden track with the door behind him, now fully in view instead of buried in the meadow; still wrong: the foreground lies in deep shade and his coat reads flat and faceted.

Brack lying in the sun on the trodden track before the white cottage: he reads as a low black-and-white dog lying down, but he is small, in the shade of the tall foreground grass, and the near grass is a dark wall.
Moonlit night at Edda's cottage with fireflies over the meadow; Brack asleep by the door under the bench is only a dim dark shape and the foreground is crushed black.
Osric, the new stone-cottage villager, tending his garth at 15.5 h with Edda beyond the field gate; FAIL: the foreground is in deep shade and his pale hood reads as a veil over his face.

Osric on his step at 07:00 with his own face for the first time: a nose and a grizzled grey beard under the hood instead of the face cloth; FAIL: the skin is a flat orange mask, the eyes glint red and the beard reads as grey bark, not hair.

Osric leaning on the garth wall at 09:30 with the hens and his stone cottage behind; FAIL: his head bows so far that the hat brim hides his face, and the forearm wraps read as blocky cylinders over the cope.
The hens have drifted over to peck round Osric's boots while he tends the sunlit garth; still wrong: he wears the hero's wide straw douli and a pale hood that reads as a mask, and stands stiff.
Osric leaning on the garth wall at 9.5 h, close up: broken -- an oversized hat brim hides the bowed head entirely, the forearms are blocky stubs, and the cope stones are blurry at this range.

Osric at his door at 07:00 with an older, paler skin in place of the orange mask; FAIL: the beard (this frame from before the re-tune) reads as a flat white plaster patch, an eye still glints red and armour shows at the collar.

Osric leaning on the garth wall at 09:30, head now lifted to look out over the field, hens on the garth, the vale and peaks behind; FAIL: he is too small and side-on to read his face, and the forearm wraps are still blocky.
Edda at the garth wall and Osric in the garth turned to each other mid-exchange at 16.4 h; both are small and the dry-wall foreground is in deep shade.
Osric on his step at 7 h with a dark hood (no more pale ski mask) and the new felt hat, which still reads as a tall stovepipe; red eye glint, flat beard and collar armour still show.

Osric at his door at 07:00 in the reworked felt hat (low round crown with a crease, drooping 9 cm brim, sat down on a dark hood); the face is still in deep shade under the brim, the beard reads as flat grey bark and armour shows at the collar.

Osric at his door at 07:00 with a stronger face fill under the felt brim: his face, nose and eyes finally show, but the lightened beard reads as a pale flat block with a ruled lower edge and a grey plate still shows under it.

Osric's beard now ends in a ragged soft point under the chin with thinning strand tips instead of a ruled rectangle; it still reads too pale and flat against the dark hood, and grey plates still show on his chest below the mantle.
Osric at his door at dawn in a wool smock (no more armour plates on his chest) with a beard in locks; the beard is still too yellow-brown with wood-grain-like strands and the smock a little bright.

Osric at his door at dawn with a cooler ash-grey beard (yellow only at the lip) and a darker wool smock; the beard still shows fine vertical streaks, the felt hat reads orange-brown and cowboy-like, and the cape looks smooth.
Osric at his door at dawn: the felt hat is darker, matte and droops all round now, but still reads warm brown, and the cape is smooth and plasticky.

Osric at his door at dawn: the felt hat is a cooler dark grey-brown and the cape shows wool fibre instead of plastic, but the brim still curls up at the sides and the cape and beard carry fine vertical streaks.
A red kite pulls up from its stoop over the meadow with four rooks mobbing it from below; the birds read, but the frame is mostly empty sky and one cloud shows a hard straight top edge.

Osric at dawn by his cottage: the felt brim now droops all round like a slouch hat and the wool cape has lost its wood-grain streaks, but the beard still shows fine vertical streaks and the skin reads flat orange.

Wat the pedlar, creel of dyed cloth bolts on his back, on the green by the lantern post at 09:24; still wrong: his face reads as a dark mask under the hat, the staff does not show, the lens catches him from the side and Brack the dog blocks the foreground.
Wat the pedlar walks the new two-rut cart track through the meadow toward the village green; the rut beds are a touch too smooth and even in tone, wanting stones and scuffs.
A red kite shrieking as it climbs away from four mobbing rooks over the meadow at 11:00; still wrong: an empty flat sky with the birds as tiny silhouettes, no landscape to anchor the frame.

Brack the collie stands stiff-tailed on the green watching Wat the pedlar after woofing at him; the low lens sits in tall grass whose blades read as flat paper ribbons, and a flat grey wall edge intrudes at the right.

Wat the pedlar walking off the green past the lantern post, bending his line round Brack sat in his road; still wrong: the lens frames him half behind the post with the dog lost in tall grass, near grass blades read as flat paper ribbons and the figures read blocky at this distance.

Wat walks the cart track toward the village with daisies and buttercups now edging the verge; the taller yarrow and knapweed of the verge ribbons are mostly drowned in the ripe grass, so the verges do not yet read as a distinct flowered strip.

Wat walks the cart track toward the village; the verges either side of the ruts are now cropped to a short green turf so the daisies and buttercups stand over it as a clear ribbon against the ripe meadow; near-lens grass blades still read as flat ribbons and the yarrow/knapweed are sparse in frame.

Wat walks the cart track in; a mossy field stone now lies on the left verge and another on the right, and wheel-scoured pebbles show in the right rut, though the rut cobbles are sparse and read as dark dots rather than a stony bed; near-lens grass still flat ribbons.

Low lens in the meadow behind Brack the collie watching Wat: the near grass now shrinks into the sward close to the camera and shows rolled, ribbed blades instead of hand-sized paper ribbons; still wrong: a grey slab at the right frame edge, HUD bars on, the dog reads a little flat.

The new squeeze stile in the garth's back wall seen from the fell footpath: two leaning slabs with a worn path through the slot toward Osric's cottage; still wrong: the slot reads wider than a real squeeze stile, the wall courses look too regular and tiled, and the light is flat.

The squeeze stile in the garth's back wall from the fell footpath: two leaning gritstone slabs with their tops rubbed bare by hands, a beaten path through the slot, no HUD bars; still wrong: the slabs' narrow faces read plain grey and the wall's dark joints form a regular grid.

The garth wall from the fell footpath with the new chip-and-moss hearting and uneven head joints; the joints still read as a near-black grid behind pale stones, and a figure stands in front of the stile.

The garth wall and squeeze stile from the fell footpath at mid-morning: face stones now butt on tight beds in varied greys with dark crust patches, no longer pale tiles on a black joint grid; still wrong: the stones read as too-regular rectangular blocks, the cope is a uniform green moss band and the slabs' faces are plain.

The garth wall's stones now split askew with leaning head joints, thin slates and a few knocked cope stones, and the cope moss is broken into cushions; the cope still reads as a row of similar upright slabs and the near face stones are still too boxy.

Garth wall squeeze stile at 10:00: the cope now rises and falls in runs with leaning stones and blocky capstones instead of a row of like slabs; the near face stones on the right still read as pale boxy blocks with sharp arrises.

Garth wall by the squeeze stile at 10:00: field stones now rounded, chipped rubble in darker greys; the cope now reads as rounded mossy lumps rather than split slabs and the far-left run's faces are still flat tiles in a regular grid.

Osric out past the garth's back wall at 17:00, standing on the fell footpath where his flock grazed, the stone cottage behind: a living moment, but he reads stiff and underlit in the sunset shade and his face reads as a pale mask at this distance.

Osric squeezing through the stile in the garth's back wall at 16:54 on his way out to the fell, the stone cottage in low sun behind: reads as a real field wall and a man using it, but he is side-on and dark against the shadowed wall, and the cope still reads as rounded lumps.

Osric on the fell footpath at 17:00 with his new weathered, wind-reddened face under the brim and a soft, swaying stance; still a fail: a pale grey strip runs down from his jaw (grizzled beard/smock side-on) and his hand raised to the brim does not show from this lens.
Osric's face portrait at 17:00 before the fix: the 'pale strip' under his jaw is his beard, a 20 cm flat grey plate hanging down his chest; his face above it is a reddish mask.

Osric's beard is now short and full, tapering to a point and shaded at the sides and underneath; still a fail: his face is a flat reddish mask with no eyes showing under the brim and the hood frames it like a helmet.

Osric's face at 17:10 with a greyer, less ruddy skin, darker sockets and lighter brow and cheekbones; still a fail: the eyes sit in the brim's shade so the face reads as a nose and beard in a dark hood.

Osric at 17:10 with the felt hat tipped back and an eye-level fill: his eyes now show as two lit slits under the brim; still a fail: the hood is a stiff box round a small face, the beard reads pale and the cape is flat wood-grain cloth.

Osric at 17:10: the beard is now dark grizzled grey with clumped locks and the cape has lost its wood-grain rings; still a fail: from the front the hood still frames the face as a squarish opening and the cape is now a plain, untextured-looking brown.

Osric at the garth in late sun: his hood now hangs askew with a worn uneven rim and his wool mantle carries road dust and wear; his face still reads as a smooth mask and the mantle is still too clean-edged.
Osric bent to the hen house at dusk as he drops the pop-hole slide; the sun is already down so the frame is near black, only his hat and the ladder show against the fireflies.

Wat the pedlar on the cart track at dusk, his horn lantern lit at his knee throwing a warm swinging pool on the ruts; still wrong: the lens catches his back not his face, the horn panes blow out flat orange, and a flower stalk cuts the foreground.

The fox up the hens' ladder at Osric's hen house, nose to the shut slide in failing light; the pose reads, but the scene is very dark and the fur is a smooth saturated red with no visible pelt detail or dark stockings.
Same moment at 19:54 from the garth: the hen house and ladder read against the moonlit trees, but the fox is only a red smear in the dark.

Wat walks the cart track at dusk with his horn lantern now glowing a soft amber, fireflies over the meadow; seen from behind, the scene beyond the lantern pool is nearly black and the pool reads as a red-brown smear.

Fur pass on the fox at Osric's hen ladder at 17:24: the coat is now a muted ginger-brown with combed tufts and no red glow, but Osric happens to be standing in front of it, so the fur is barely seen and needs a clean night re-shot.

Osric woken at 01:30, out at the gap in the yard wall with his horn lantern lit and warm light on the wall stones; but the lantern hangs at his waist instead of held up, his face is lost under the brim, and the moonlit night reads flat blue-grey rather than Wukong-dark.

Osric at the yard-wall gap at 01:30 now holds his lit horn lantern up before his chest and its warm light falls on the wall stones; but his face is still a dark smudge under the brim, his coat reads flat pale grey, and the moonlit night is flat blue.

Osric at the yard-wall gap at 01:30 with his lantern held up: its glow now lights his face and beard from below, Brack sits at his knee and only a few fireflies remain; still wrong: a dark raised fist beside his face, the whitewashed cottage glows too bright and blue for the small hours, and his coat reads flat pale grey.

Osric at the yard-wall gap at 01:30 with the lantern held out to his side, fist clear of his face, under a greyer, less blue moon; still wrong: his face falls dark again, the raised open hand reads like a wave, the coat is flat pale grey.

Osric at the yard-wall gap at 01:30 with his fingers now closed into a fist round the lantern bail and the lantern hanging below it; still wrong: his thumb hooks out toward his face, his face under the brim still reads dark, and the coat is flat pale grey.

Osric at the yard-wall gap at night: the lantern's glow now reaches his cheek and the underside of the brim, but his thumb still sticks out sideways off the bail like a hitch-hiker's and the face is still mostly shadow.

Osric at the yard-wall gap at 01:30 with the lantern's glow now leaning up toward his face, so his face and beard read warm under the hat brim; still wrong: a hard bright band lights the brim's underside, the coat is flat pale grey with no weave, and the right-hand wall stones show orange-red patches.

Osric at the yard-wall gap at 01:30 with his lantern fist after the thumb-wrap change: the hand reads as a fist, but at close range the thumb still pokes out sideways from its top, his face is a dark mask under a bucket-like hat, and the right-hand wall stones still carry orange-red patches.

Osric at the yard-wall gap at 01:30 with his lantern held up: the glow on his hat brim is dimmer and narrower than before, but a bright streak still crosses the brim's front, his face is still mostly shadow, the hat reads like a bucket and the thumb pokes up.

Osric holding his lantern up at the yard-wall gap at night: the bright band across his hat brim has shrunk to a small warm spot at the left edge, but his face is still mostly shadow and the hat still reads as a bucket.

Osric at dusk with his reshaped felt hat: the crown now tapers into a pinched, slumped dome and the brim snaps down front and back instead of a straight-sided bucket; his face is still mostly shadow and the crown still stands a touch tall.

Osric at 17:10 after the wool-cape weathering pass: only a faint sun-faded grey reads across the top of the cape, the damp hem and mud flecks are out of frame, and the cape still reads as one smooth sheet with a bucket-ish hat and a shadowed face.

Osric full figure at 17:10 after deepening the wool cape's folds: a few vertical fold shadows now break the cape, but the whole figure still reads pale grey and flat against the dark field, the hem detail is lost at this range, and the frame is underlit.

Osric at 17:10 with a darker oiled-wool cape and smock and a lower hat crown: he now sits into the field instead of reading as a pale grey cut-out, but the ochre rope girdle is now the brightest patch on him, the cape still reads flat, and the pose is stiff.

Osric at 17:10 with his rope girdle and shin wraps dulled to old grey-brown hemp and mud-greyed linen: the bright ochre band at his waist is gone, but he still reads as a stiff dark mannequin and the cape's right edge juts out sideways like a stiff flap.
Osric at dusk: his wool cape now falls plumb down his stooped back instead of jutting out behind like a stiff pointed flap; still a stiff dark figure with his face a dark mask under the brim.

Osric on the fell at 17:10 from 2.3 m with his wool cape now falling close down over the shoulders and arms: the stiff pointed flap that stood out at his side is gone, but the pale armour still shows down his chest, his face is a dark mask under the brim and the pose is stiff.

Osric idling at his cottage door at 07:12 with his weight on one foot: the stone cottage, hill and sky read well, but he stands in deep shadow by the door and the frame is badly underexposed, so the figure is a dark silhouette.

Osric by his door at 07:12 with the new low-sun exposure: wall stones, his cape and the path stones now read where the previous frame was near black; the foreground grass and yard floor are still too dark and he stands in flat profile.

Osric by his door at 07:12 with the new low-sun skylight on open ground: the sward by the wall now reads green and the yard floor is a shade lighter than in osric-morning, but the foreground path and grass roots are still too dark and he is a flat dark profile.

Osric's yard at 07:12 with the low-sun ground fill raised: the foreground seed heads and the sward by the wall read brighter, but the earth round the path stones and the cottage's lower wall are still near black.
Osric's yard at 07:12 with paler trodden earth behind the path stones; the stones and the shaded foreground are still near black.

Osric's yard at 07:12: the door stones now read as pale worn slabs and the wall tops are lifted by the low-sun skylight, but the earth between the stones, Osric's pale figure and the frame's overall exposure in the cottage's shade are still too dark.

Osric's yard at 07:12: the dirt cracks round the path slabs are a touch browner instead of black, but the shaded foreground, the wall foot and Osric's dark coat still sink, so the frame reads underexposed.

The hero climbing the watchtower keep's outer face at 10:30, arms up on the stones: climbing now works, but the pose is a stiff procedural reach with no hands planted on the stones, the cape hangs dead straight and the masonry reads too clean and blocky.

The hero on the keep face with the hands now planted on the stones, elbows bowed out like a climber's; from below the hands hide behind the hat, the cape still hangs dead straight and the masonry reads too clean and blocky.

The hero climbing the keep face from the side: one knee is drawn up and the foot is planted on a stone below. The red cloth still hangs dead straight off the wall, the masonry is too blocky and clean, and the camera sits too far behind to show the hands.
The climbing hero's red robe panel now drags toward the drawn-up knee instead of hanging dead plumb; at this range the figure is small and the keep masonry still reads blocky and clean.

The hero climbing the keep, whose stones now vary from pale buff to dark weathered grey, with frost spalls and black-green drip stains under each course; the masonry still reads as stacked rectangular blocks and the camera still sits behind the hero.

The climbing hero on the keep from a raking angle: face stones now set proud or sunk back and some cut short under dark open joints, with crisper arrises; the camera still sits mostly behind the hero and the moss on the stone tops is a flat green.

The climbing hero on the keep after the moss pass: the flat green slabs on the stone tops are gone, but the moss is now too sparse to read as cushions, and the camera still sees the hero mostly from behind.

The hero climbing the keep, re-aimed from their facing after warm-up: the frame now shows the staff, sash and hands on the stones, but the lens still sits behind the shoulder, the bed tops are above eye level so the moss cannot be seen, and the stones read pale and flat like plaster blocks.

The hero on the keep from above along the face: the stone tops now show their moss and the faces in shade read darker and greyer, but the sunlit faces still look pale and soft, the hero is still seen from behind, and the moss reads as a dull flat green from this distance.

The hero gliding over the vale under Caelum's new hemp-and-bamboo glider, rigging cords and bank visible, the village and snow peaks ahead; the canopy still reads as one flat even brown sheet (patches, seams and battens too faint) and the hero hangs only a few metres over the rising hill.

The hero under Caelum's hemp-and-bamboo glider over the Vale at 10:30: the wing reads as a real swept glider at the right scale against the body, but the canopy is a flat even brown with its patches and battens lost at this range, the hero hangs stiffly straight down, and the meadow below is sparse and soft.

The hero gliding high over the vale: the canopy now reads as sewn cloth, with panels from different bolts, pale rubbed batten ridges, a dark tarred leading edge and a stitched ox-blood patch, but the undyed panel glares near white in the sun (since toned down) and the figure under the wing is still a small, stiff silhouette.

The folded glider rides across the hero's back as a cord-bound canvas roll with bamboo ends; it sits too high above the sash, the staff crosses over it and its pale batten bands glare (lowered and dulled after the shot, not re-shot).

The hero circles under the glider in the thermal over the keep's knoll at 14:00, heading toward the sun over the dry vale; the wing and the light hold up, but the rising chaff that marks the column is invisible at this range and the meadow below is sparse.

The hero glides over the vale with both legs trailing back, knees bent, and the madder robe panels streaming out behind in the airflow; the canopy still reads as stiff flat cards from this angle and the straw hat and sash rim look flat-shaded.

The hero gliding over the dry vale at 14:00: the canopy now arches and its panels belly up between the battens instead of reading as a flat card, but the pale linen panels glow near-white from below and the lens caught him from astern, not the side.

Caelum's glider from the front quarter at 14:00: the wing arches and the panels belly between the battens, the linen bolts are duller but still read pale in full sun; the sky's cloud layer ends in hard vertical seams and the trailing legs smear grey.

Same glide framing as the last shot after the camera far-plane fix: the cloud deck now runs unbroken across the sky with no seams; the trailing legs below the robe still read as a pale grey smear and the hero is small in frame.

Same framing as glide-sky: the hero's trailing legs now read as dark hemp thigh bindings and road-soiled shin wraps instead of a pale grey smear; the hero is still small in frame and the meadow below is thin.
Close crop of the trailing legs under the madder robe panel: worn brown cloth, no grey smear; at this distance the wrap spirals and the bare feet are still mushy.

Hot still afternoon on the meadow: a dust devil stands up ~30 m beyond the hero, but it reads as a thin faint wisp of smoke, not a spinning column of dust; the hero is small and the grass in front is fine.
Crop of the whirl: a pale narrow funnel with a little skirt at its foot; it needs to be two to three times wider and denser, with a darker, more opaque base.

Same glide framing as legs2: the meadow beyond the grass clumps now reads as rough tussocky grassland with tan seed-head drifts instead of smooth olive felt; still thin trees and no tall grass past 64 m.
Crop of the lower-left meadow: metre-wide tussocks with dark gaps and bleached tops; at this crop the mottling is a bit uniform and speckly.

Same devil framing as devil2: the dust devil ~30 m out now reads as a tall tan column of churned soil with a dense dark skirt at the foot instead of a faint wisp; the hero is still stylized and the straw post odd.
Crop on the whirl: soft billowing funnel flaring toward the top with a soil-dark base; still reads a bit like smoke, needs visible spin streaks and more debris.

A dust devil 12 m off the hero (devil spot, near): a tan whirling column rising from the track, now with visible spin striations; its skirt is hidden by the tall grass and the hero still looks stylized.
Crop on the whirl: the throat shows horizontal streaks of dust dragged round the column, so it reads as spinning rather than smoke; the top still dissolves into a soft haze and few straw flecks show.
A dust devil 12 m off the hero with dead leaves and chaff now whirling round and flung out of the column; the hero still looks stylized and the skirt hides in the tall grass.
Crop on the whirl: brown tumbling leaves read clearly against the sky and the bowl keeps a firmer right edge; the top still melts into a soft haze against the cloud.

Glide view over the vale after 240 more oaks were added in the outer groves: hardly different from the 11:15 frame; the far floor still reads as scattered lone trees, and the hero still looks stylized.
Ground view past the dust devil: the middle distance still shows open meadow with lone oaks, no woodland edge; the new outer woods don't read in this framing.

Same glide framing as 16:50 after the outer oaks were packed into six woods: a dark closed wood now fills the right middle distance, but the centre (the inner vale round the village, first-pass lone oaks) still reads as parkland and the hero still looks stylized.
Crop on the right half: the crowns now merge into one dark canopy mass instead of separate lone trees; the wood edge is soft and the crowns still look thin and acacia-like up close.

The vale from the glider after the lone meadow oaks were thinned (compare 1800-outer-woods-air2): the middle ground is now open field with a few clumps and a dark wood edge on the right, not savanna; the oak crowns still read thin and acacia-like from above and the meadow is a flat olive.

From the village garth a new oak copse now stands in the right-hand middle ground in front of the far wood, but its crowns are still thin and see-through, more acacia than oak, and the meadow is one olive tone.

From the village the near copses and far woods now read as full, dense oak crowns instead of see-through acacias; the crowns still sit a little flat-topped and dark-uniform, and the meadow is one olive tone.

Village at 14:00 with the new field patchwork: greener cropped pasture and gold hay strips now break the meadow round the cottage, but the middle ground past 80 m still reads mostly one olive-tan and the oak crowns one dark green.

Village at 14:00 with per-tree leaf casts and a sunlit crown skin: the near copses are fresher green with paler tops and the right-hand wood shows a few different crowns, but from 80 m the woods still read mostly one dark green and the crowns are flat-topped.

Village view with doubled per-tree crown casts: the right-hand wood now shows yellow-green and darker crowns side by side, but the woods past 80 m are still mostly one green and the crowns sit flat-topped.

Village view with lobed oak crowns: the right-hand oaks now show paler domed caps over darker skirts and fuller canopies, but the far woods are still one soft green mass and the domes read only faintly.
Village view with stronger lobed oak crowns: the right-hand oaks now break into several shaded domes with dark creases; crowns still dull olive and the left wood reads as one dark mass.

Village view with field tints raised at distance: the middle ground past 80 m now breaks into green pasture, gold hay and brown fallow patches instead of one olive-tan; crowns still dull olive and the hero is not in frame.

The hero at noon by the training post with the sash now a muted, creased cloth band (wound twice, knot and tails on the far hip) instead of a flat bright-yellow ring; the indigo hood still reads as a flat box and the straw hat as a plain cone.

Head-and-shoulders of the hero at noon: the hood is now faded slate-blue wool with drape folds and shaded valleys over the shoulders, and the straw hat has a tied crown peak and a rolled, bound rim; the hat still reads too bright and smooth a yellow, and the face looks doll-like.

The hero's straw hat now reads as a weathered herringbone plait of split cane, a muted brown with sun-greyed patches instead of a smooth bright-yellow cone; the face still reads doll-like (wide round eyes) and the face cloth flat.

Hero at noon: the face cloth is now darker damp wool with vertical folds that set it apart from the slate hood; still wrong: the eyes read round and doll-like and the chest plate's pale edge wear looks painted on.

Hero at noon: the eyes now sit narrower with a smaller iris tucked under a lash-shadowed upper lid and a duller white, no longer doll-like; still wrong: the face reads smooth and young, and the chest plate's pale edge wear looks painted on.

Hero at noon: the eyes now sit as narrower almond eyes under a dark upper lash line with a smaller iris and duller whites instead of round doll eyes; still wrong: the chest plate's pale edge wear looks painted on and the brow above the eyes is a featureless band.

Hero at noon after the armour-wear rework (satin lacquer, chips thinned, rim wear from the normal map); at this range the change barely shows and the torso still reads as pale linen wraps and a brown mantle, not dark lamellar.

Hero at noon by the training post: the forearm wraps now read as road-soiled linen, not pale cuffs; the chest and shoulder plates and the bare hand still read pale grey-tan and the face is too small to read.

Hero at noon by the training post after recalibrating the armour masks: the chest, shoulder and arm plates now read as dark lacquered lamellar instead of pale grey-tan; the lacquer is close to flat black at this range, the pale hood dominates, and the face is too small to read.
Hero at noon with the hood darkened from pale slate-blue to greyed wool and a slightly lifted lacquer; the armour still reads as one near-black mass at range and the face is lost under the hood.

Hero at noon with warmer black-brown lacquer and more sheen on the plate fields: the torso now reads dark brown with faint shoulder-plate shading, but the plates still merge at this range and the face is lost in the hood's shade.
Before (left, 16:26) and after (right): the lacquer is a step warmer and the shoulder plate catches a little sky; plate separation is still weak.

Hero at noon with dark creases between the lacquered plates and the texture's baked plate shading carried into the lacquer: the road, fields and farmhouse read as a place, but at this range the plates still merge and the face is lost in the hood's shade.
Before (left, 17:25) and after (right): the plate creases are only faintly visible at 6-8 m; the thigh and knee plates gained a little shape, the torso barely changed.

Hero's face at noon with the meadow's ground bounce now lighting the skin under the hat brim: eyes and cheeks read inside the hood, but the skin is still smooth and young and the dark armour merges into one mass.
New 2 m hero lens at noon: the face under the hood now gets the meadow bounce fill like his armour, but the frame still reads game-like (blocky training post at left, dull figure).
Face crop: warm skin and an eye now read inside the hood instead of a black slit; the skin is still smooth and the eye small at this range.

Practice post at noon beside the hero: now a hewn, tapered oak post with a rounded top under a dark iron band and a lashed straw bundle; the meadow still lacks depth haze and the hero reads small and dull.
Post top x4, first pass (left) vs darkened iron (right): adze flats, drying checks and a rain-rounded top replace the turned cylinder; the band is still a touch light in full sun.

Hero at the 2 m lens at noon with the hewn oak post in the foreground: the post now reads as adzed timber under an iron band, but the face is still a small patch in the hood and the plain meadow lacks depth haze.
Face x5, before (left) vs after (right): deeper sockets, a lighter brow bone and sun-mottled cheeks give the face some bony structure, but at this range it still reads soft.
